item.title: Sri Lanka Customs’ October revenue exceeds target by 4.9-pct
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: It has achieved 8.3 percent more than this year’s target in the first 10 months.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka Customs exceeded its October target by 4.9 percent, while revenue in the first 10 months of 2026 jumped around 15.9 percent compared to the same period last year, official data showed.

Customs’ October revenue target was set at 193.3 billion rupees. However, the revenue-collecting body collected 202.7 billion rupees that month, exceeding the target, according to official data.

It also exceeded the cumulative target for the first 10 months by 27.5 percent, achieving 2,336 billion rupees.

Last year, Customs collected a record 2,551 billion rupees in revenue, exceeding a revised target of 2,241 billion rupees for the year and achieving 64.2% higher revenue than the previous year’s revenue of 1,553 million rupees.

Customs set a revenue target of 2,207 billion rupees for this year, 13.5% less than last year as it expects a significant decline in car imports. Data showed it achieved 8.3 percent more than this year’s target in the first 10 months.

Analysts expect the revenue collecting body to achieve fresh record high revenue this year, surpassing the last year’s one.

Sri Lanka Customs’ revenue jump is largely due to stronger enforcement, improved valuation practices, and a rebound in import volumes after years of contraction.

Following the 2022 economic crisis, imports fell sharply as the country imposed restrictions to conserve foreign exchange.

However, with the stabilization of reserves, the relaxation of certain import controls, and a steady recovery in consumer demand, customs collections from import duties, excise, and other levies have risen.

Officials note that tighter monitoring of under-invoicing and misdeclaration of goods has also contributed to boosting state revenue.

The combined effect of increased import activity, currency movements, and stricter enforcement has positioned Customs as one of the top revenue sources for the Treasury in 2025, providing a vital cushion as the state works to meet fiscal targets under the IMF-supported program. (Colombo/November 11/2026)

item.title: Dialog Axiata Sept quarter net profit surges 62-pct to Rs9.25bn
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Supported by continued expansion in data and home broadband demand.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka telecommunications giant Dialog Axiata PLC recorded a group net profit of Rs. 9.24 billion for the quarter ended September 30, surging 62.4 percent from Rs. 5.69 billion in the same quarter last year, interim accounts showed.

Basic earnings per share rose to Rs. 1.00 for the September quarter, up from Rs. 0.62 a year earlier.

Quarterly revenue grew 6.2 percent to Rs. 48.54 billion from Rs. 45.69 billion, supported by continued expansion in data and home broadband demand.

Direct costs fell 4.7 percent to Rs. 20.21 billion from Rs. 21.21 billion on cost efficiencies, lifting gross profit by 15.7 percent to Rs. 28.33 billion.

While administrative expenses rose 13.5 percent to Rs. 9.63 billion and distribution costs edged up 1.3 percent to Rs. 4.98 billion, net impairment losses on financial assets dropped 61.8 percent to Rs. 270.8 million on improved credit collections.

Operating profit jumped 27.9 percent to Rs. 13.47 billion from Rs. 10.53 billion.

Finance costs plunged 42.0 percent to Rs. 1.91 billion from Rs. 3.29 billion, aided by active balance sheet deleveraging that trimmed total group borrowings to Rs. 64.11 billion by September 30 from Rs. 76.49 billion at end-2025, alongside lower domestic interest rates.

Although net foreign exchange losses widened 132.8 percent to Rs. 917.7 million from Rs. 394.1 million, overall net finance costs fell 25.5 percent to Rs. 2.64 billion.

Pre-tax profit climbed 54.9 percent to Rs. 10.84 billion, while income tax expense rose 22.2 percent to Rs. 1.59 billion.

Total assets stood at Rs. 287.17 billion as of September 30, with net asset value per share at Rs. 9.99. Contracted capital expenditure commitments jumped to Rs. 15.71 billion from Rs. 6.30 billion at end-2025.

On September 30, the group amalgamated five subsidiaries—including Digital Commerce Lanka and Dialog Device Trading—into Digital Holdings Lanka, and merged My Health Solutions into Digital Health under a legal entity simplification drive.

In October, Dialog sold a 20 percent stake in Digital Health to Sunshine Healthcare Lanka and Nawaloka Hospitals for Rs. 374.9 million, reducing its holding to 44.05 percent and reclassifying it as an associate.

The board proposed an interim dividend of Rs. 0.70 per share.

Dialog shares closed at 45.80 rupees at the end of September and were trading around 49.70 rupees today.  (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka’s Odel Sept quarter net loss widens 8.4-pct to Rs704mn
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Anchored by its core fashion retail segment which generated Rs. 1.71 billion or 92.7 percent of external turnover
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka fashion retailer Odel PLC recorded a group net loss of Rs. 704.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, widening 8.4 percent from a loss of Rs. 649.3 million a year earlier, interim accounts showed.

The group posted a basic loss per share of Rs. 1.31 for the September quarter, compared to a loss of Rs. 1.21 previously.

Quarterly revenue rose 13.5 percent to Rs. 1.85 billion from Rs. 1.63 billion, anchored by its core fashion retail segment which generated Rs. 1.71 billion or 92.7 percent of external turnover, alongside Rs. 134.4 million in commission and rental income.

However, cost of sales surged 23.4 percent to Rs. 972.0 million from Rs. 787.7 million, outpacing revenue growth and squeezing gross margins from 51.6 percent to 47.4 percent.

Gross profit rose just 4.3 percent to Rs. 875.0 million from Rs. 839.0 million.

Operating loss widened 27.6 percent to Rs. 270.5 million from Rs. 212.0 million as administrative expenses climbed 11.2 percent to Rs. 1.07 billion, outweighing an 8.6 percent drop in distribution expenses to Rs. 75.9 million and Rs. 3.5 million in other income.

Finance costs edged down 1.3 percent to Rs. 434.7 million from Rs. 440.7 million—still absorbing nearly half of gross profit—while finance income fell 64.2 percent to Rs. 1.2 million.

Company balance sheet and cash flow figures point to active debt reprofiling into longer-term maturities.

Non-current borrowings jumped 37.5 percent year-on-year to Rs. 15.42 billion as of September 30, while short-term borrowings fell 30.1 percent to Rs. 6.10 billion following Rs. 4.21 billion in first-half medium- and long-term loan drawdowns used to pay down short-term debt and halve bank overdrafts to Rs. 983.8 million.

Short-term dues to related parties also rose 27.3 percent to Rs. 7.02 billion, reflecting ongoing parent-group funding support.

Notes showed subsidiary Odel Properties One (Pvt) Ltd has completed Rs. 7.58 billion of work under its Rs. 9.81 billion Ward Place development (New Odel Mall) contract with China Construction Third Engineering Bureau, alongside Rs. 4.50 billion in non-contracted capital commitments.

Notes also highlighted a 1.19 percent public float—below regulatory minimums—with Softlogic Retail Holdings owning 98.79 percent, while first-half guarantee fees to the ultimate parent dropped to Rs. 9.2 million from Rs. 53.0 million.

Total assets stood at Rs. 32.78 billion, while accumulated losses of Rs. 16.34 billion deepened negative equity to Rs. 6.30 billion, leaving net asset value at negative Rs. 11.70 per share versus negative Rs. 7.68 a year earlier.

Odel shares closed at Rs. 10.70 at the end of September and are currently trading around Rs. 13.00–13.20.  (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka president reviews final 2027 Budget proposals ahead of presentation
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Dissanayake will present the complete budget proposal tomorrow afternoon (12) in his capacity as the Minister of Finance
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has reviewed the final draft of the 2027 Budget proposals ahead of its official presentation to Parliament tomorrow afternoon, his media division said.

The review session was attended by Finance Ministry Secretary Harshana Suriyapperuma.

Shifting the national economic focus from stabilization to aggressive expansion, the 2027 Budget features 2,000 billion rupees allocation dedicated exclusively to capital expenditure, the president’s media division said.

Dissanayake will present the complete budget proposal tomorrow afternoon (12) in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka central bank flags Crosslink for unauthorized deposit-taking
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: With Crosslink Holdings, continued collecting public funds by masked loan agreements and fixed deposits
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has issued a public warning declaring that Crosslink Investment (Pvt) Ltd and Crosslink Holdings (Private) Limited operated unauthorized deposit schemes.

Following an investigation under the Finance Business Act No. 42 of 2011, the banking regulator determined that Crosslink Investment illegally took public deposits between April 2020 and January 2022.

The entity, alongside its sister firm Crosslink Holdings, continued collecting public funds through August 2022 by masked loan agreements and fixed deposit contracts.

Both companies have been ordered to halt all finance business operations immediately.

The CBSL has identified six directors and managers tied to the unauthorized operations: Wanasinghe Mudiyanselage Jaliya Kamal Wanasinghe, Wanasinghe Mudiyanselage Sanjaya Kamal Wanasinghe, Wanasinghe Mudiyanselage Udara Kamal Wanasinghe, and Kirage Premalatha (Directors), alongside Rajapakshage Sachini Madhukala Rajapaksha (Director – Operations) and Dissanayake Mudiyanselage Anjula Sandeepani Dissanayake (Finance Manager). (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lank regulator restricts specific Ernst & Young partners following NDB fraud
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: CBSL clarified that restriction applies specifically to Engagement and Quality Assurance partners involved in NDB audit
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s central bank (CBSL) has asked audit firm Ernst & Young, Sri Lanka (E&Y) to block the engagement partner and the quality assurance partner involved in the audit of the National Development Bank’s financial statements from handling any future commercial banking audits.

The directive follows the exposure of a 13.6 billion rupee internal financial fraud at NDB.

While targeting individual accountability, the regulator emphasized that E&Y remains a qualified auditor approved to service licensed banks under the Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988.

The CBSL statement is reproduced below:

Clarification on the Auditors to Audit the Accounts of Licensed Banks in Sri Lanka

Following the disclosure of an internal fraud at National Development Bank PLC (NDB), the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) requested M/s Ernst & Young, Sri Lanka (E&Y) not to assign any audit engagements of Licensed Banks to the Engagement Partner and the Quality Assurance
Partner involved in the audit of NDB’s financial statements.

For the avoidance of doubt, this restriction does not affect the recognition of E&Y as a qualified auditor eligible to audit the accounts of Licensed Banks in Sri Lanka under the provisions of the Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988, as amended.
(Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka launches 5-day business name registration pilot
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: 3-month pilot across 20 selected Divisional Secretariat divisions in the Central, Northern, North Central, and North Wes
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka has launched a pilot project to replace its century-old business name registration process with a simplified, unified system that cuts registration time to just five days.

The Simplified and Unified Business Name Registration (BNR) pilot was launched in Anuradhapura on November 10.

The programme is being carried out by the Ministry of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development in partnership with the Chrysalis institute and provincial councils.

It aims to streamline the registration of sole proprietorships and partnerships, introducing a single uniform procedure across the entire island.

“The main objective of the reform is to reduce administrative barriers for those planning to start a business and for small and medium-scale entrepreneurs, enabling them to enter the formal economy more easily,” Deputy Minister of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe said.

Sri Lanka’s business name registration framework, which has been in place since 1918, required applicants to provide documents proving land ownership and obtain approvals from multiple institutions.

Under the reform, business name registration will be separated from the process of obtaining other legal licences.

The new procedure will rely only on basic identity and residence details.

“Entrepreneurs will no longer need complex land ownership documents, as registration will now be based solely on basic identity and residence details to complete approvals within five days,” a ministry official said.

The initial phase will run as a three-month pilot across 20 selected Divisional Secretariat divisions in the Central, Northern, North Central, and North Western Provinces.

Once the pilot is evaluated, the government plans to expand the unified system island-wide and introduce a digital platform to make the service even more efficient in the future. (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Thilina Panduwawala appointed executive director of Sri Lanka’s Frontier Research
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Since October 2025, Thilina has served as Senior Consultant to Parliament’s Committee on Public Finance.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Frontier Research has appointed economist Thilina Panduwawala as Executive Director, effective 1 January 2027 where he will lead the firm’s strategy and research agenda.

“His mandate is to deepen the conviction of its macroeconomic research on Sri Lanka, strengthen relationships with institutional investors, boards, treasury teams and trading desks, and develop Frontier Research’s next generation of research talent, the firm said.

The appointment marks Thilina’s third stint at Frontier. Recruited and trained by the firm’s late founder, Amal Sanderatne, he first joined in 2016, where he embedded political analysis into the firm’s forecasting.

After 18 months with the Asian Development Bank’s Sri Lanka Resident Mission, he returned in 2022, during the economic crisis, and led the firm as Head of Research through the sovereign default and debt restructuring.

He steered Frontier’s views on the exchange rate, interest rates and inflation through the rupee’s collapse, record inflation and policy tightening, and then through the domestic debt optimisation and the restructuring of Sri Lanka’s external debt.

Since October 2025, Thilina has served as Senior Consultant to Parliament’s Committee on Public Finance.

There he has supported the Committee’s oversight of fiscal and monetary policy across Budget 2026, the ongoing Budget 2027, and the fiscal packages that followed Cyclone Ditwah and the Middle East conflict.

“The role has also given him a view from inside the fiscal machinery of the State, the economy’s single largest participant.”

“Thilina has seen Sri Lanka’s economy from every vantage point that matters: a multilateral lender at the ADB, investors and treasury teams at Frontier Research, and now the State’s finances from within Parliament. That breadth, together with the rigour Amal instilled in him, makes him the right person to lead Frontier Research into what will be its strongest chapter yet,” Frontier Research, Director, Chanakya Dissanayake said.

Amal Sanderatne founded Frontier’s Macroeconomic Research Service on the conviction that getting the macro call right is essential to superior investment returns in Sri Lanka.

Founded in 2003, Frontier delivers independent, high-conviction macroeconomic research for institutional investors, boards, treasury teams and trading desks.

It serves as a macro research provider to most of the country’s asset managers and banks. (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka and Italian chambers sign deal to boost trade
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Ceylon Chamber secures new institutional link to Italy’s business network through Unioncamere Agreement
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce and Unioncamere, the Italian Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Handicraft and Agriculture have signed an agreement providing Sri Lanka businesses wider access to the Italian market.

“The agreement establishes a framework for direct engagement between the business communities of the two countries, with a focus on trade promotion, investment opportunities and business collaboration,” the chamber said.

The agreement provides a direct institutional link to Italy’s extensive chamber network, creating opportunities for Sri Lankan companies to identify business partners, explore market opportunities and establish commercial relationships.

Planned areas of cooperation include business delegations, B2B matchmaking, knowledge exchange and the promotion of trade and investment.

Through its Sri Lanka–Italy Business Council, the Ceylon Chamber will work to translate the agreement into greater business engagement, opening further avenues for Sri Lankan companies to connect with Italian counterparts and explore opportunities in the Italian market. (Colombo/Nov11/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka hopes to fully utilize Rs.2,000bn capital spending next year
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Cabinet Spokesman admits 2026 capital investment can't be fully utilized
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – The Sri Lankan government has adjusted its procurement cycles for development projects with the hope of utilizing the full Rs. 2,000 billion capital expenditure planned for next year, Cabinet Spokesman Nalinda Jayatissa said.

The island nation’s successive governments have failed to utilize the capital spending every year due to delays in approvals, tender process and procurements.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s government has spent only less than 25 percent of the allocated Rs. 1,340 billion in the first nine months of the year, Finance Ministry officials have said.

“Spending 100 percent might not be possible in this year due to various technical reasons. In some places there were issues with tenders; in some places there were issues in the procurement process,” Jayatissa, also the minster of health and media, told reporters at the weekly Cabinet media briefing.

He said the government, however, has urged the ministries not to wait until January of next year to initiate these development projects.

“If you plan to start in January, you will only be able to actually get it underway around May,” he said.

“Now you know that funds will be allocated. The plans that respective ministries submitted to the Ministry of Finance knows about those plans. They have an idea of how much money will be spent. Accordingly, several steps including preparing plans, preparing estimates, and initiating procurement activities can be carried out even before the budget is passed.”

“(Ministries can) carry out the procurement activities, and wait until the budget is passed only to award the contract.”

“Once the budget is passed this time on December 14th, and after the Speaker signs it, generally within the month of December there is the ability to know the amount of money allocated to one’s ministry. Then, awarding can be made starting even from the first week of January, if needed.”

“It is that very process that we have granted approval for across all ministries. It is along with that that we expect to spend this 2,000 billion.”

Sri Lanka’s chronic failure to utilize its full budgetary allocations for capital investment reflects deep-rooted structural inefficiencies in public financial management and project execution, analysts and economists say.

They warn of lower economic growth in the future if the government fails to implement its planned capital investment projects.

The government has repeatedly said most of the spending occurs in the last quarter of the year.

Year after year, bureaucratic delays, protracted procurement disputes, politicized project selection, and a lack of technical expertise within line ministries leave a significant portion of capital expenditure unspent on the Treasury books.

This capital under-utilization carries severe long-term repercussions for the island’s economic trajectory.

By failing to deploy allocated funds into critical infrastructure such as transport networks, modernized power grids, and digital public systems, Sri Lanka suffers from lower productivity growth and worsening structural bottlenecks as well as a decline in overall gross domestic product (GDP) potential.

In a fragile post-default macroeconomic climate, this persistent shortfall also sends a negative signal to international development partners and private investors.

It demonstrates an institutional inability to absorb capital effectively, thereby stalling the very structural transformation required to safely out-grow a historic debt burden.

President Dissanayake last month promised to change the process to fast-track the spending. (Colombo/November 10/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka Cabinet approves $200mn ADB loan for MSMEs
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: The Department of External Resources has concluded formal loan negotiations with the ADB to acquire the funds.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka’s cabinet has approved entering into an agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to obtain a 200 million US dollar loan to support micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).

The facility will finance ‘Sub-program 1’ of the Sector Development Program, which focuses on building a robust and inclusive financial ecosystem for MSMEs.

The Department of External Resources has concluded formal loan negotiations with the ADB to acquire the funds.

The 200 million dollar loan will be drawn from the ADB’s ordinary capital resources and is divided into two equal tranches of 100 million US dollars each.

One tranche will serve as policy-based lending, while the other provides financial intermediation lending.

The financing falls under a broader framework approved on March 16, 2026, to conduct negotiations for up to 620 million US dollars across five sub-programs to support Sri Lanka’s reform agenda aligned with the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Extended Fund Facility.

Responding to questions from journalists on why Sri Lanka is securing 200 million dollars after seeking approval for 620 million dollars, cabinet spokesperson Nalinda Jayatissa clarified:

“Approval has been granted for the entire 620 [million]. Accordingly, depending on how negotiations progress and based on the case we present, the loan is disbursed,” Jayatissa said.

Jayatissa noted that discussions were held to secure the 200 million dollar loan under two distinct repayment frameworks.

The 100 million dollar policy-based component carries a 12-year repayment period with a three-year grace period.

The remaining 100 million dollar financial intermediation component has a 15-year repayment period alongside a five-year grace period. (Colombo/Nov10/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka shares jump 2.75-pct on lower oil prices, US election tariff hopes
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Easing global pressures and lower oil prices helped lift market sentiment
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s Colombo Stock Exchange closed sharply higher on Tuesday, CSE data showed, with the benchmark All Share Price Index moving up 2.75 percent.

The ASPI was up 592.02 points at 22,123.39, while the more liquid S&P SL20 was up 3.66 percent, or 224.97 points, at 6,368.12.

Easing global pressures and lower oil prices helped lift market sentiment, Raynal Wickremeratne, Head of Research and Strategy at NDB Securities, said.

“One of the things in the past that were dragging the market down was oil prices and also the negative sentiment globally. I think now some of that sentiment has recovered, you’re seeing oil also coming down, and effectively when you look at Sri Lanka, oil is one of the biggest factors here more than anything else,” Wickremeratne said.

He added that investors were also hopeful that shifts in power in the US House and Senate could lead to potential adjustments in US trade tariffs, providing relief to emerging markets with heavy US tariff burdens.

Positive contributors to the ASPI were Vallibel One (up 6.14 percent at 95.10 rupees), Dialog Axiata (up 4.88 percent at 49.40 rupees), Commercial Bank of Ceylon (up 4.28 percent at 225.25 rupees), Hayleys (up 4.02 percent at 239.25 rupees), and Hatton National Bank (up 3.81 percent at 415.00 rupees).

Softlogic Life Insurance (down 4.98 percent at 78.30 rupees), Softlogic Capital (down 4.17 percent at 11.50 rupees), Ambeon Holdings (down 3.28 percent at 35.40 rupees), LOLC Finance (down 1.96 percent at 5.00 rupees), and Ceylon Cold Stores (down 1.38 percent at 125.00 rupees) were top negative contributors.

Market turnover was 7.96 billion rupees. The banking sector led turnover with 2.03 billion rupees.

Several crossings were recorded during the session, led by Dialog Axiata (800 million rupees), Commercial Bank of Ceylon (309 million rupees), John Keells Holdings (93.7 million rupees), Swisstek (56.1 million rupees), Commercial Credit and Finance (52 million rupees), CAL Closed End Fund (50 million rupees), and Seylan Bank (50 million rupees and 39.2 million rupees).

Other notable crossings included DFCC Bank (41.2 million rupees), D Products (40.8 million rupees), Nations Trust Bank (28.2 million rupees), Ceylon Cold Stores (25 million rupees), CIC Holdings (21.5 million rupees), Hemas Holdings (21.4 million rupees), Sunshine Holdings (21.3 million rupees), Chevron Lubricants Lanka (21 million rupees), and Access Engineering (21 million rupees).

Dialog Axiata generated a combined 1.4 billion rupees of total turnover, driven by 800 million rupees in crossings and over 600 million rupees on the open market. (Colombo/Nov10/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka awards Rs1.73bn contract to build Kelaniya University complex
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: The new building will house the university’s Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka’s Cabinet has approved awarding a 1.73 billion rupee contract to M/s Sathuta Builders (Pvt) Ltd to construct a 10-storey building for the University of Kelaniya.

The new building will house the university’s Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies, reviving a project that was earlier halted due to the country’s economic crisis.

The approved contract sum excludes Value Added Tax (VAT).

The procurement began after the Cabinet granted approval on February 3, 2025, to resume the project through national competitive bidding, attracting a total of 10 bids.

“Following the evaluation of the bids, the contract is awarded to the lowest substantially responsive bidder based on recommendations from the procurement committees,” minister Nalinda Jayatissa said. (Colombo/Nov10/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to build new Mahaweli rail bridge under Indian credit line
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: The historic "Black Bridge" (Kalu Paalama) restoration will proceed in parallel.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s cabinet has approved a proposal to build a new railway bridge across the Mahaweli River between Sarasavi Uyana and Peradeniya, with financial assistance from an Indian credit scheme, minister Nalinda Jayatissa said.

The new bridge on the Matale railway line forms part of an initiative to develop an extensive suburban railway network covering the Kandy municipal area, where a feasibility study is currently underway.

Under the scope of the project, authorities plan to double-track the main railway line from Kadugannawa to Gampola via Peradeniya, and double-track the Matale line from Peradeniya to Katugastota.

Jayatissa noted that these measures are required to complete the planned double-tracking, eliminate bottlenecks caused by existing single-track sections, and improve the reliability and connectivity of the network.

“This project aims to restore and develop railway infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Ditwah and will enable the integration of the Matale railway line into the national railway network,” Jayatissa said.

Responding to questions from reporters on whether the new bridge would halt work on the historic “Black Bridge” (Kalu Paalama), Jayatissa said restoration on the older bridge will proceed in parallel.

“The restoration works will not be stopped,” Jayatissa said. “It is alongside that, that work is being undertaken regarding the construction of this bridge.”

Jayatissa explained that the single-track Black Bridge, originally built in 1865, suffered significant damage during the cyclone.

Due to its age and structural limitations, the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau (CECB) is carrying out the repairs with technical assistance from the University of Peradeniya.  (Colombo/Nov10/2026)
